column2: Retain Levi's Gedson, Kaath and Merari as the new selected chapter opening. The repetition of 5:27 remains and is not deleted or renumbered.
Retain the names heading and Gedson's Lobeni and Semei. Both names remain distinct from later differently formed entries in related lines.
Retain Kaath's Ambram, Issaar, Hebron and Oziel. No name is changed to reconcile the later Amminadab chain.
Retain Merari's Mooli and Omousi and the repeated ancestral-families formulation. The repetition is in the selected heading rather than an English duplication to remove.
Retain the dative framing for Gedson and for Lobeni his son, followed by Jeeth and Zemma with son links. The compressed hierarchy is not converted to a new explicit begetting sequence.
column3: How does the repeated dative framing relate Jeeth to Lobeni and Gedson in this selected construction?

column2: Retain Joach, Addi, Zara and Jethri with each his son. The successive relationship markers remain rather than a list of siblings.
Retain Kaath's sons heading, Amminadab, Kore and Asir with son links. Amminadab is the selected name here and is not replaced by Issaar from the later singer genealogy.
Retain Elkanah, Abiasaph and another Asir in the continuing son chain. The repeated Asir is not silently removed.
Retain Thaath, Uriel, Ozia and Saul, each his son. The terminal Saul is not identified with the king merely because the English name matches.
Retain Elkanah's sons Amasi and Achimoth. The following his son sequence remains connected without supplying a missing father name.
Retain Elkanah, Souphi and Naath with three son links. No repeated opening Elkanah formula from another witness is inserted.
Retain Eliab, Jidaer and Elkanah, each his son. This selected list is not harmonized to the differently formed ascending genealogy later in the chapter.
Retain Samuel's firstborn Sani and Abia. Sani is not silently replaced by Joel from verse 18 or parsed as a second-son label without a textual decision.
column3: What does the selected Sani form represent, and how does it relate to the firstborn designation?

column2: Retain Merari's Mooli and the chain Lobeni, Semei and Oza. The semicolon distinguishes the opening descendant from the subsequent son links.
Retain Somea, Aggia and Asaia with each son relation, completing this Merarite chain. No singer's genealogy is substituted for it.
Retain David's appointment over the singers' work and the ark coming to rest. Work interprets the hand-related agency construction contextually, not as a separate object explicitly named in Greek.
column3: Does over the work of the singers best express the selected appointment phrase?

column2: Retain instrumental ministry before the tent of the house of testimony, its endpoint at Solomon's Jerusalem building and service according to prescribed order. Instruments are explicit here; prescribed order is the inherited contextual rendering of krisis.
Retain the stationed ministers and sons from Kaath, Heman as psalm singer and descent through Joel to Samuel. Joel is preserved here despite the earlier Sani firstborn notice.
Retain the ascending chain Elkanah, Edad, Eliel and Thie. Its selected name forms are not rewritten to match verses 11–12.
Retain Souph, Elkanah, Meth and Amasias with each son-of link. The repeated Elkanah names in the wider chain remain.
Retain Elkanah, Joel, Azariah and Saphania as the next four ancestors. No generation is omitted to simplify the genealogy.
Retain Thaath, Asir, Abiasaph and Kore. This ascending order is not rearranged to the earlier descending list's sequence.
Retain Issaar, Kaath, Levi and Israel, closing Heman's genealogy. Issaar here remains distinct from Amminadab in verse 7.

Retain brother Asaph standing at his right and the Barachia/Samaa lineage. Brother may be broader Levitical kinship or colleague language; the different genealogies do not require silently changing the noun.
Retain Michael, Maasia and Melchia in Asaph's ascending chain. These names are not identified with unrelated holders elsewhere.
Retain Athani, Zarai and Adia with repeated son-of links. The selected forms remain without automated normalization.
Retain Ethan, Zamma and Semei as the next three ancestors. Zamma is not silently changed to the earlier Zemma form.
Retain Hecha, Gedson and Levi to close Asaph's lineage. The terminal Levi marks the broader kinship with the other singers.

Retain Merari their brother's sons on the left and Ethan descended through Kisai, Abdi and Maloch. The right/left arrangement remains, and brother is not narrowed to an immediate sibling relation between singers.
Retain Asebi, Amessia and Chelkios in Ethan's ancestry. The Greek selected names remain distinct from similar priestly names.
Retain Amasai, Bani and Semmer with their son relations. No familiar form is substituted solely from another genealogical list.
Retain Mooli son of Mousi son of Merari son of Levi. The selected chain is not altered to make Mooli and Mousi siblings on the basis of verse 4.
column3: How should this chain be understood alongside the earlier parallel sons heading without silently reconciling the witnesses?

column2: Retain the Levite brethren by ancestral houses assigned to all the tent ministry's work. All belongs to the work's scope rather than an invented universal priestly role.

Retain Aaron and sons offering on both the whole-burnt-offering and incense altars, Holy-of-Holies work, atonement for Israel and Moses's commands. Burned incense is the inherited rendering of thymiontes across both altars, but its breadth remains a lexical question.
column3: Should the first altar require a broader burn-offerings rendering of thymiao rather than incense at both locations?

column2: Retain Aaron's sons heading and Eleazar, Phinees and Abisou in successive son links. The genealogy repeats part of chapter 5 without omission.
Retain Bokai, Ozi and Zaraia with each son relation. No alternate priestly spelling is introduced in this repeated list.
Retain Mariel, Amariah and Achitob in the sequence. The recurrence of familiar names is not sufficient grounds for merging generations.
Retain Sadok and Achimaas, closing the priestly chain at its selected endpoint. Later descendants from chapter 5 are not appended.

Retain dwellings, villages and boundaries, Aaron's Kaathi family and the explanatory lot. The English integrates the parenthetical allotment statement without claiming a first lot absent from this selected wording.
Retain Hebron in Judah and its surrounding lands all around. Surrounding lands is the inherited provisional rendering of perisporia, preserving repeated spatial scope.
column3: Does perisporia here specifically denote pasture, cultivated environs or a broader land allotment?

column2: Retain the city plains and villages assigned to Caleb son of Jephonne. These are distinguished from the preceding Levitical allotment without asserting a modern property division.

Retain the plural cities-of-refuge heading, Hebron, Lobna, Selna and Esthamo and the repeated surrounding lands. The English follows the selected list without supplying the more limited refuge-city classification of another account.
column3: How far does the plural refuge heading govern the following city list?

column2: Retain Jeththar and Dabir, each with surrounding lands. The repetition marks separate allocations rather than redundant phrasing to delete.
Retain Asan, Attan and Basamys, each with surrounding lands. No missing or alternate city is substituted to reconcile the subsequent total.

Retain Benjamin's Gabee, Galemeth and Anchoch, their lands and the stated thirteen-city total. The preceding selected list supplies twelve named entries; the total remains unreconciled rather than adding a thirteenth city.
column3: Does an apparatus or differently divided place name explain the discrepancy between the list and thirteen?

column2: Retain the remaining Kaathites, ancestral families, the repeated from-the-tribe expression, half Manasseh and ten cities by lot. The awkward repeated tribal phrase is not filled with an inferred missing tribal name.
Retain Gedson's family allocation from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Manasseh in Basan, with thirteen cities. No half modifier is added here merely because verse 56 later specifies half Manasseh.
Retain Merari's allotment from Reuben, Gad and Zebulun and twelve cities by lot. The tribal order and total are not altered to fit the later shorter named list.
Retain Israel's sons as donors of both cities and surrounding lands to the Levites. The collective action does not newly identify which individual named each city.
Retain Judah and Simeon, the lot and the singular he called by name. Benjamin is not imported into this shorter selected list and the unnamed singular naming agent remains.
column3: Who is the singular naming agent, and would passive wording obscure a meaningful selected distinction?

column2: Retain some ancestral families of Kaath's sons receiving territorial cities from Ephraim. Some represents the partitive from-the-families opening without implying an exact number of recipient families.
Retain singular him, plural refuge cities, Sychem in Mount Ephraim and Gazer, each with lands. The recipient is not silently pluralized to resolve the collective reference.
Retain Jekmaam and Baithoron with their separate land allotments. No Upper/Lower specification is supplied for Baithoron.
Retain Eglam and Gethremmon, each with lands. The selected cities are not replaced by more familiar forms from another allotment account.
Retain half Manasseh's Anar and Jeblaam with lands and the remaining Kaathite family recipient. Eight named cities in verses 52–55 are not expanded to force the earlier total ten.
column3: How does the selected named list relate to the ten-city summary, and what textual evidence explains its shorter extent?

column2: Retain Gedson's sons, families of half Manasseh, Golan in Basan and Aseroth with lands. The half modifier is explicit here and stays distinct from verse 47.
Retain Issachar's Kedes and Deberi, each with surrounding lands. Kedes here is not merged with the later Galilean Kedes merely because the name recurs.
Retain Dabor and Anam with lands, completing four named Issachar allocations. The names remain the selected forms.
Retain Asher's Masal and Abaran with separate lands. No alternate coastal identification is inserted into the reading text.
Retain Ikak and Roob with lands, completing the Asher sequence. The repeated allotment formula remains.
Retain Naphtali's Kedes explicitly in Galilee, Chamoth and Kariathaim, all with lands. This completes the thirteen named Gedson allocations without conflating the two Kedes locations.
Retain Merari's remaining sons, Zebulun's Remmon and Thachchia and their lands. Only the two selected names are listed; no additional Zebulun cities are restored from another witness.
Retain beyond Jordan at Jericho, west of Jordan, Reuben, Bosor in the wilderness and Jasa with lands. The selected west is not corrected to east from geographical expectations.
column3: How does west of the Jordan qualify the preceding Jericho/beyond-Jordan expression in the selected text?

column2: Retain Kademoth and Mophaath with lands in the continuing Reuben group. The first two cities and these two complete the selected four without extra locality descriptions.
Retain Gad's Ramoth Galaad and Maanaim with separate lands. The named Galaad qualification remains with Ramoth.
Retain Esebon and Jazer with lands to close the chapter. The later Merari lists name ten cities while verse 48 states twelve; no additional cities are invented to harmonize the count.
column3: What textual or list-division evidence explains the difference between the twelve-city summary and these ten named allocations?
